technique: right-handed cross-hand default with note-value-aware sticking and phrase-aware exceptions
authorityPolicy: Per-note sidecar is authoritative. Renderer must not guess when an assignment exists.

BD.reason: Main bass-drum pedal under right foot on standard right-handed setup.

LP.reason: Project label explicitly defines LP as left-foot hi-hat.

LB.reason: Project label explicitly defines LB as left-foot bass drum.

SN.startHandPolicy: Choose a single-stroke alternating start hand phrase-by-phrase; prefer R lead, but choose parity/start so the final hand leaves the immediately following required cymbal/tom hand available. Respect simultaneous-hand conflicts and the authoritative M1-16 precedent.

LC.reason: Preserve existing project right-handed cymbal convention; phrase solver may override only to avoid impossible simultaneous conflict.

TOMS.reason: Use relaxed alternating single strokes for tom fills; restart R after phrase break.

simultaneousPolicies.assignment: must use distinct hands; resolve by instrument-side preference and phrase continuity
feet do not consume hand availability

researchReferences.title: Drumeo - How To Play Drums
researchReferences.note: Standard setup places bass drum at right foot and hi-hat pedal at left foot.

researchReferences.title: Drumeo - Latin grooves
researchReferences.note: Examples use right hand on ride/cowbell, left hand around snare/toms, left foot on hi-hat.

researchReferences.title: Vic Firth - Fresh Approach to Drumset sampler
researchReferences.note: Tom single-stroke exercises use R-L alternation.

rhythmicStickingPolicy.meaning: For repeated strikes on the same hand-played part, eighth-note spacing remains on the normal/default hand when practical; sixteenth-note-or-faster spacing becomes an alternating-sticking candidate.
exceptions: Simultaneous hand-played notes must use distinct hands.
Phrase continuity may choose the starting hand so the following required strike remains playable.
Tom traversal may retain alternating hands at slower spacing when alternating is more natural for moving across the kit.
Do not alter chart note timing, part, or instrument to satisfy sticking.
